$comment: Assembly jigs built and drawn by tools/jigs.py under ce-cad/bin/cad. Every contact diameter is derived from a MEASURED bearing ring boundary or a measured seat — the sources are named in the module docstring and repeated in each row's `basis`.

microduck-jig-press-22-outer.title: Bearing press pusher — 22x16x4 outer ring into a Ø22 printed bore (trunk_base hip-yaw, head head-roll)

geometry.contact_on: outer ring; flat at the face over Ø20.000-21.500 (z=0.05 : (8.15,9.0),(10.0,10.75) -> bore chamfer 0.2, OD chamfer 0.3)
geometry.cage_note: the cage band sits at bearing MID-height (Ø18.690-19.290, seen only in the mid-plane slice) and the face slice shows no material between the two rings, so the cage is unreachable: this tool's face rests ON the ring face and no part of it enters the bearing.
geometry.rule: load path: pusher -> outer ring -> printed bore. The relief bore Ø18.600 stands clear of the inner ring (Ø18.0) at the face, so nothing crosses the balls.

sliced.basis: the slicer's OWN result.json numbers, never derived from volume

microduck-jig-press-22-inner.title: Bearing press pusher — 22x16x4 inner ring onto a Ø16 printed boss (yaw2roll Ø16.0x1.95, hip-bracket Ø16.0x1.95, yaw-roll-motion Ø16.0x4.0)

geometry.contact_on: inner ring; flat at the face over Ø16.300-18.000 (z=0.05 : (8.15,9.0),(10.0,10.75) -> bore chamfer 0.2, OD chamfer 0.3)
geometry.rule: load path: pusher -> inner ring -> printed boss. The land is a plain Ø18.0 boss standing 2.5 mm proud of the Ø26.0 grip body, so the outer ring (Ø22.0) and the cage never touch this tool. Centring is by the Ø16.400 pocket over the part's own boss.

sliced.basis: the slicer's OWN result.json numbers, never derived from volume

geometry.contact_on: outer ring; flat at the face over Ø13.500-14.500 (z=0.05 : (5.15,5.75),(6.75,7.25) -> bore chamfer 0.2, OD chamfer 0.3)
geometry.cage_note: the cage band sits at bearing MID-height (Ø12.198-12.804, seen only in the mid-plane slice) and the face slice shows no material between the two rings, so the cage is unreachable: this tool's face rests ON the ring face and no part of it enters the bearing.
geometry.rule: load path: pusher -> outer ring -> printed bore. The relief bore Ø12.100 stands clear of the inner ring (Ø11.5) at the face, so nothing crosses the balls.

sliced.basis: the slicer's OWN result.json numbers, never derived from volume

geometry.contact_on: inner ring; flat at the face over Ø10.300-11.500 (z=0.05 : (5.15,5.75),(6.75,7.25) -> bore chamfer 0.2, OD chamfer 0.3)
geometry.land_rim_verdict: FAIL for FDM at a 0.4 mm nozzle: 0.550 mm is under the 0.80 mm two-perimeter floor. Machine this one.
geometry.rule: load path: pusher -> inner ring -> printed boss. The land is a plain Ø11.5 boss standing 2.5 mm proud of the Ø26.0 grip body, so the outer ring (Ø15.0) and the cage never touch this tool. Centring is by the Ø10.400 pocket over the part's own boss.

microduck-jig-horn-zero.title: XL330 horn-at-centre go/no-go gauge — two Ø1.5 pins on the Ø12 tapped circle, arm referenced to the top of the case (+9.5 above the horn axis)

pins.into: the horn's 4 x Ø1.6 tapped holes, FACE_PCD = 12.0, FACE_AT = ((0,6),(0,-6),(6,0),(-6,0)), FACE_DEPTH = 6.0

geometry.datum_face: gauge z = 0 = the Ø16.0 horn disc face (servo x = 14.5)

reference_face.surface: the top of the XL330 case, BODY_Z[1] = +9.500 above the horn axis

geometry.witness_window: 4.0 x 4.0 through the foot at gauge z = -8.5 .. -4.5, so the operator sees the case face and any gap under the reference
geometry.absolute_zero: CANNOT DETERMINE — no fetched ROBOTIS source states the horn's angular datum relative to the case, so this gauge fixes an INDEX, not an absolute 2048. The line records Present Position(132) at the gauge as the unit's horn-zero offset.
geometry.use: command Goal Position 2048, drop the gauge on the horn with both pins engaged, check the foot sits flat on the case top through the witness window, then read and record Present Position(132).

sliced.basis: the slicer's OWN result.json numbers, never derived from volume

microduck-jig-press-anvil.title: Press anvil / nest — Ø24 through bore, Ø30x2 shoulder relief, vice slots

geometry.use: the part lies on this face with the seat over the Ø24 bore, so the bearing has somewhere to go and the press load lands on the part's own seat boss rather than on a printed wall.

sliced.basis: the slicer's OWN result.json numbers, never derived from volume

jig_set_total.note: one printer, one set of jigs; sequential per-piece times, a plate prints faster than the sum
